title: Joint aspiration (draining fluid from a joint)
what: The doctor uses a thin needle to draw out extra fluid from a joint. This reduces swelling, and the fluid can be sent for testing.
why: For a swollen joint, to find the cause: inflammation, gout, infection or injury. Sometimes medicine is injected at the same time.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the fluid test takes from one day to several
tell_doctor: Allergy to local numbing or iodine
Fever or a skin infection over the joint
Diabetes - if steroids will be injected

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you can eat as normal.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes, so the joint is easy to uncover.

bring: Scans and ultrasound of the joint
steps: You lie or sit and the joint is placed comfortably
Your skin is cleaned with antiseptic
The doctor puts the needle into the joint, often guided by ultrasound
The fluid is drawn into a syringe, and sometimes medicine is injected
A plaster is put over the needle spot
feel: Pressure in the joint during the tap
Afterwards the swelling usually goes down and the joint moves more easily
after: Go easy on the joint for a day
If medicine was injected, rest for a day or two
You can apply cold through a cloth if your doctor allows it
Discuss the fluid test results with your doctor
red_flags: Fever, or the joint becomes hot and red
Severe pain or swelling that grows

faq.a: Sometimes. It depends on the cause, which is why the fluid test matters.
Usually it is bearable. The skin is numbed, and what is unpleasant is mainly the pressure.

reminders.text: Joint aspiration tomorrow. Take your scans and wear loose clothes.
